decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approaches with open grippers; orient toward left rear and right front supports, using small continuous increments.
Align open fingers over the two chosen supports, then descend conservatively; block centers estimated from calibrated head RGB.
Use wrist-image centering corrections, then close both grippers on the support blocks. Retention remains to be checked by lifting.
Lift both supports upright and begin moving them inward on their own sides; keep grippers closed and verify retention in RGB.
Bring retained supports to opposite ends of the planned lower layer, then lower them upright to table height.
Set down and release the base supports. Withdraw upward and outward before reorienting for a two-arm grasp of the long board.
Rotate to opposing end grasps of the lower board while clear of the supports, then approach its ends with open fingers.
Replan from interrupted pose with smaller rotations; finish alignment and descend gradually to the long board's ends.
Close both end grasps and lift the lower board level, keeping both grippers fully closed; inspect retention before translating over the supports.
Carry the retained board level over the two base supports and lower slowly toward their tops, preserving symmetric end grasps.
Release the lower board on the upright supports, then clear it upward and outward. Begin turning toward the remaining middle-layer blocks.
Approach the two remaining white blocks from above, finishing front-facing gripper alignment. Leave a small vertical margin for wrist-camera correction before closing.
Center each remaining block in the wrist view, descend the final small distance, and close both grippers without moving the blocks laterally.
Lift the grasped middle supports clear of the table, then carry them inward above the completed lower board; maintain upright orientation and closed grippers.
Position the middle supports symmetrically over the lower board, compensating for the right grasp offset, and lower upright toward contact.
Release both middle supports on the lower board, lift clear, and withdraw toward the nearer board while beginning opposing end-grasp orientations.
Approach the middle board with open grippers, slowly rotating toward symmetric end grasps while descending clear of the tower.
Finish matching opposing end-grasp orientations, lower to the middle board, and close both grippers. Check the board remains level during the next lift.
Lift the middle board level with closed end grasps, reaching clearance above the upright middle supports before carrying it forward.
Carry the retained middle board level over the two middle supports, maintaining clearance and symmetric closed grasps.
Lower the middle board gently onto both upright supports, then open both grippers while keeping the board centered.
Withdraw clear of the completed middle layer. Park the left arm on its own side and turn the right gripper toward the small wooden top board.
Bring the left arm toward home without crossing the tower. Approach the small board from the right workspace with an open front-facing grasp and a remaining height margin.
Finish returning the left arm home. Center and lower the right fingers around the small wooden board, then close for a test lift.
Test retention of the small top board by lifting straight up with the right gripper closed; keep the left arm at home and inspect for slip.
The small board is visibly retained. Rotate it horizontally to match the tower while carrying it inward above the completed middle layer, staying on the right side.
Center the small board over the middle layer, finish its horizontal yaw alignment, and descend conservatively while keeping the grasp closed.
Make the final centering adjustment and lower the small board onto the middle layer, then release and withdraw upward on the right.
Leave the released top board undisturbed. Move outward above the right workspace and orient for a side grasp of the remaining green top piece.
Descend toward the green piece from its right side with open fingers, using the wrist image for final alignment before grasping.
Use the wrist view to center the green top piece between the right fingers, close, and make a small vertical test lift to check retention.
The green piece appears retained between the fingers. Lift upright to clear the tower, then begin carrying it inward with the right gripper closed.
Carry the visibly retained green piece over the small top board, staying in the right workspace and leaving clearance for final centering and descent.
Correct the green piece slightly leftward over the small board and lower slowly toward its surface, retaining the grasp until final alignment is checked.
Seat and release the centered green top piece, then withdraw upward and to the right without touching the completed tower. Keep both grippers open.
The released tower remains upright in RGB. Return the right arm toward home along an outward, rearward path, retaining elbow-up continuity and open grippers.
Continue returning the right arm smoothly toward its original pose, clear of the stable tower; both grippers remain open.
